evidence: Cic. Off. 1.20: jūstitiae prīmum mūnus est ut nē cui quis noceat nisi lacessītus injūriā
terms.comment: Justice as a virtue: cōnstāns et perpetua voluntās jūs suum cuique tribuendī (Just. Inst. 1.1.1, Lewis & Short). In the Vulgate also righteousness. Injustice is injūstitia (Traupman 154). The courts and the law are jūdicia and jūs (see court, law).

evidence: Cic. de Or. 1.240: prō aequitāte contrā jūs dīcere (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Fair dealing, which looks to goodwill where jūstitia gives only what is strictly due, so that one can plead it against the letter of the law; sometimes simply justice. Its first sense is evenness, and aequitās animī is calm of mind (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: jūstitiae prīmum mūnus est ut nē cui quis noceat nisi lacessītus injūriā
phrases.english: the first duty of justice is that no one should harm anyone unless provoked by a wrong

phrases.latin: fundāmentum autem est jūstitiae fidēs, id est dictōrum conventōrumque cōnstantia et vēritās
phrases.english: and the foundation of justice is good faith: keeping to what has been said and agreed, and truth in it

phrases.latin: ut forīs ita domī, ut in magnīs ita in parvīs, ut in aliēnīs ita in suīs agitāre jūstitiam
phrases.english: to practise justice at home as abroad, in small things as in great, with one’s own as with others’

phrases.latin: remōtā itaque jūstitiā quid sunt rēgna nisi magna latrōcinia?
phrases.english: take away justice, then, and what are kingdoms but robbery on a grand scale?
